<!-- generated from maestro item 1421 — do not edit; the board item is the source of truth -->
Tenants can optionally delegate ACME DNS-01 once by publishing a permanent _acme-challenge CNAME to a target allocated by the dnsman federation hub. dnsman then issues and renews apex-plus-wildcard certificates through the hub without tenant DNS credentials or further tenant DNS changes. Existing Route53/GoDaddy DNS-01 and Maestro Sites HTTP-01 remain unchanged and enabled.

---

## Spec

Kind: feature · Requested by: Ian Starnes · Dependencies: #1422 hub, then #1423 client transport

### Acceptance criteria

- Delegation is opt-in. Missing hub configuration disables only delegation initiation; direct Route53/GoDaddy issuance remains the default.
- Initiation accepts an existing permission-checked Domain or a tenant group plus normalized external name, persists an immutable local client_ref before the first network call, and returns the hub-assigned permanent CNAME source/target.
- Pending external names do not reserve globally unique Domain.name. Verification creates Domain(provider="mojo") only after authoritative exact one-hop CNAME proof and an active tenant group check under lock.
- Local targets/client_ref values are tenant-bound tombstones, never reused after deletion. Later hub replies must match the immutable stored target.
- Pending delegation never changes a direct domain's issuance path. Federated routing becomes sticky after first successful delegation verification; broken verified delegation fails closed with no fallback.
- Delegated v1 accepts exactly apex plus wildcard. Both ACME digests are published together through #1423 at the opaque hub target and propagation probes that target.
- Alias verification occurs before every ACME order. Missing, changed, chained, or conflicting aliases consume no CA order.
- Publish cleanup intent is recorded before the remote call, so an ambiguous success/timeout still triggers idempotent withdrawal in finally.
- Certificate request/renewal is serialized and deduplicated. A transient delegated renewal failure preserves the still-valid active certificate/material and schedules bounded retry/backoff.
- Existing certificate custody, KMS/material endpoint, jobs and sync payload remain unchanged.
- REST exposes only permission-gated initiate/status/verify state; no hub zone id, API key, foreign target, TXT digest, PEM, or private key.
- Tests cover tenant isolation, target non-reuse, group deletion/inactivity, raw-name claim races, CNAME proof, optional/direct compatibility, concurrent issue jobs, ambiguous remote writes, renewal preservation, and apex/wildcard grouping.

### Public tenant API

- POST /api/dnsman/delegation/initiate with either {"domain": id} or {"group": id, "name": "example.com"}.
- GET /api/dnsman/delegation?domain=id and GET /api/dnsman/delegation/<id>.
- POST /api/dnsman/delegation/verify with {"delegation": id}.
- GET /api/dnsman/config adds delegated_acme availability, CNAME record type, returned target suffix, apex_wildcard profile, and requires_provider_credentials=false.
- Public states: pending, verified, broken. Retired tombstones are never serialized.
- Certificate request remains the existing asynchronous endpoint.

### Persistence

Create AcmeDelegation with nullable Domain relation, tenant/user snapshots, immutable tenant identity snapshot, normalized domain_name, UUID client_ref, immutable hub target/source, pending/verified/broken/retired state, timestamps and stable error code. Used rows are retained as tombstones. New schema requires an owner-authored migration unless the owner explicitly authorizes Codex to create it.

### Challenge

| Objection | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Original plan duplicated the hub Route53 zone/writer in #1421 | Amended: #1422 exclusively owns zone and writes; #1421 uses #1423 only. |
| Pending mode could unexpectedly replace direct DNS | Amended: pending is inert; sticky remote routing starts only after verification. |
| SET_NULL tenant deletion could create a house Domain | Amended: verify locks and requires the original tenant still active, otherwise retires/refuses. |
| Concurrent jobs can overwrite certificate state/material | Amended: atomic issue claim, request deduplication and concurrency tests are required. |
| Renewal failure currently strands still-valid material | Amended: preserve active material and schedule bounded retry/backoff. |
| Remote publish may succeed before a timeout | Amended: record cleanup intent before publish and always idempotently withdraw. |
